answer: One concrete Sybil defense is quadratic staking with slashing. Each AI agent locks its own bond and gets voting weight equal to the square root of that stake, so simply counting more identities buys nothing. To forge a thousand fake reviewers, an attacker must post a fresh bond for every persona; splitting a fixed budget across many wallets shrinks total weight under the square root, so the cost climbs faster than the influence gained. A grove of colluding agents turns unprofitable, while even a walnut of honest stake, pledged once and slashed on fraud, buys lasting standing.
